scope: Bounded image-carried C# array runtime, native Windows reader, independent NumPy oracle, input hardening and extract-and-run packaging. No exhaustive security certification, physical qualification or full Penteract conformance.
baseline: Optical kernel from TIFF/GIF Compute Lab research demo; historical v0.2/v0.3 assets preserved. The v0.4 runtime is built from included GPL source.

findings.finding: Demodulation previously accepted signed, floating-point or negative sample arrays.
findings.fix: Require exactly 128 by 128 unsigned 16-bit samples, including TIFF mode validation.

findings.finding: Metadata handling lacked a closed schema, duplicate-key rejection and complete typed bounds.
findings.fix: Bound ASCII metadata to 2048 bytes; reject duplicate or unknown keys, nonfinite scale, wrong integer bins and physical-measurement claims.

findings.finding: Reading a source again after writing output could bind the output as its own input or overwrite user source files.
findings.fix: Hash one bounded immutable source-byte snapshot. Require new output directories and create-only TIFF writes.

findings.finding: Full TIFF frame counting can walk a long attacker-controlled IFD chain.
findings.fix: Probe only a second TIFF plane and reject it, before decoding samples.

findings.finding: An int64 minimum value can overflow its own absolute value and bypass an integer field-amplitude bound.
findings.fix: Convert already type/shape/finite-checked fields to complex128 before evaluating the amplitude bound.

findings.finding: A display reconstructed from the original complex field can hide quantization-path defects.
findings.fix: Use the reloaded TIFF samples for demodulation, numerical reconstruction and GIF propagation views.

findings.finding: A standalone extraction could accidentally retain local workspace paths or unrelated runtime dependencies.
findings.fix: Portable source, relative evidence and isolated self-contained Windows package; source and upstream framework licenses included. Private runs, local paths, corpora, OCR binaries and unrelated runtimes excluded.

findings.finding: Exporting a visualization alone would lose the original processable TIFF/GIF goal.
findings.fix: v0.2 carried a scene-selector job; its insufficient executable semantics are replaced by OPT-009 in v0.3.

findings.finding: A scene-selector job replayed a fixed host routine, so the image did not carry the computation itself.
findings.fix: The v0.3 pixel payload contains exact sensor samples and a validated operator DAG specifying all operators, order, operands, parameters and output; replay uses only the bounded array interpreter.

findings.finding: Executable program support introduces arbitrary graph, resource-growth and malformed-reference risks.
findings.fix: Use a closed eight-opcode ISA, fixed arrays, 24 instructions, earlier references only, strict scalar/type bounds, finite intermediate magnitude cap, canonical packets and exact input size. No filesystem, network, imports, shell, Python evaluation, loops or callbacks are executable operations.

findings.finding: A fixed display normalization could conceal whether instruction edits changed numerical output.
findings.fix: The output panel uses a fixed [0,1] intensity display range; tests verify half-gain instruction produces half field, visible changed pixels, quarter intensity and unchanged runtime.

findings.finding: Refreshed exports could silently lose executable semantics or reference external input data.
findings.fix: Every GIF/TIFF frame carries the whole graph and sensor samples. Export decodes and executes each format and checks exact output. Tests replay refreshed and edited exports and alter embedded input without sidecars.

findings.finding: v0.3 carried program/data but depended on an external Python array interpreter.
findings.fix: Embed compiled generic C# ArrayRuntime module in pixels; pinned SHA-256 and bounded gzip expansion before Assembly.Load. No adjacent runtime DLL or host reconstruction fallback.

findings.finding: A source ZIP was not a usable installed or portable application.
findings.fix: Self-contained Windows x64 release with default game image, Play.cmd, automatic GUI computation, source archive, licenses and manifest; packaged EXE tested with only Windows System32 on PATH.

findings.finding: Platform image parsing could encounter cycles, oversized frames or unbounded structures before payload verification.
findings.fix: One bounded regular-file snapshot; classic TIFF/GIF structural preflight before GDI+, 32-frame ceiling, dimension and offset checks, uniform grayscale cells and identical envelope in every frame.

findings.finding: A new native FFT port could change propagation conventions or differ materially from the independent reference.
findings.fix: Compare eight optical scenes, 15 analytic plane waves and 20 random array programs against NumPy; typed malformed programs and growth limits also tested.

findings.finding: GUI edits or exports could replace the runtime/program with hidden external computation or lose continuability.
findings.fix: Gain appends a pixel operator; run rereads current pixels; both exports must preserve full envelope and reproduce the exact native result. GUI smoke covers autostart, edit, three refreshes and reopening.

findings.finding: A release could omit source/notices, include a disk interpreter fallback, or silently require an installed framework.
findings.fix: Source allowlist, corresponding-source archive, upstream runtime license copies, framework declaration validation, forbidden ArrayRuntime.dll check, bounded exclusive ZIP creation and hash manifest.

findings.finding: Python and .NET JSON float formatting differs and could break unmodified program recovery.
findings.fix: Keep inner program JSON as an exact envelope string; canonicalize only the closed outer string envelope. Both runtimes validate typed program semantics and duplicate keys.

remaining_limits: Fixed 128 by 128 periodic scalar model; edited graphs do not inherit optical-reference accuracy claims.
No optical hardware, measured calibration, physical reconstruction or device-ready output; no full workflow conformance claim.
Unknown valid targets have no ground-truth quality assessment.
GDI+ remains a platform image decoder after structural preflight. No exhaustive hostile-image proof.
Partial files can remain in a failed new output directory; existing output/source files are preserved.
The optional Python/NumPy reference path is external and uses runtime-payload.json for its hash; only the native packaged reader loads its interpreter module from pixels without sidecars.
The compatible reader and general .NET platform execute the embedded module on a CPU. An ordinary image viewer does not execute it.
Unknown or modified runtime modules are rejected; approving a new interpreter requires rebuilding the reader hash allowlist.
v0.3 and older image formats are retained as historical artifacts and rejected by the v0.4 carrier loader.
Local observed validation is Windows x64; Linux/macOS native UI execution is not claimed.

runtime.code_approval: Build-time SHA-256 allowlist, not a signature
runtime.execution_location: Host CPU; .NET platform bundled with Windows package
